payload.summary: Directive 2003/87/EC (EU ETS Phase 1 base text) grounds the scope determination (Art. 2(1), Art. 3(e), Annex I), the monitoring/reporting duty and calculation method (Art. 14, Annex IV), the surrender obligation (Art. 12(3)), and verification of material misstatement (Art. 15, Annex V). These support surfacing per-site, per-year operational fields: installation identity, reporting year, Annex I activity type, activity/energy data, emission factor, and reported CO₂e. Note that the two-method cross-check relies on GHG-Protocol 'Scope 2' (indirect electricity) figures and a 5% discrepancy threshold, neither of which are defined in this Directive — the text covers direct installation emissions and only an unquantified 'material misstatement' concept. These gaps are flagged in missing_regulatory_context.

findings.statement: The Directive applies to emissions from the activities listed in Annex I and greenhouse gases listed in Annex II.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Article 2 Scope 1. This Directive shall apply to emissions from the activities listed in Annex I and greenhouse gases listed in Annex II.

findings.statement: An 'installation' is a stationary technical unit where one or more Annex I activities are carried out, including directly associated activities with a technical connection that could affect emissions.
findings.evidence_excerpt: 'installation' means a stationary technical unit where one or more activities listed in Annex I are carried out and any other directly associated activities which have a technical connection with the activities carried out on that site and which could have an effect on emissions and pollution;

findings.statement: Annex I lists categories of activities with capacity/output thresholds (e.g. combustion installations exceeding 20 MW rated thermal input, production of pig iron or steel exceeding 2.5 t/h) that determine which installations fall within the scheme.

findings.statement: Member States shall ensure emissions are monitored per the guidelines and that each operator of an installation reports emissions from that installation during each calendar year to the competent authority.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Member States shall ensure that each operator of an installation reports the emissions from that installation during each calendar year to the competent authority after the end of that year in accordance with the guidelines.

findings.statement: Emissions may be monitored by calculation using Activity data × Emission factor × Oxidation factor; the report for each Annex I activity must include activity data, emission factors, oxidation factors and total emissions.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Calculations of emissions shall be performed using the formula: Activity data × Emission factor × Oxidation factor ... For each Annex I activity ... Activity data; Emission factors; Oxidation factors; Total emissions; and Uncertainty.

findings.statement: By 30 April each year the operator of each installation must surrender allowances equal to the total emissions from that installation during the preceding calendar year, as verified under Article 15.
findings.evidence_excerpt: Member States shall ensure that, by 30 April each year at the latest, the operator of each installation surrenders a number of allowances equal to the total emissions from that installation during the preceding calendar year as verified in accordance with Article 15

findings.statement: Operator reports must be verified against Annex V criteria; a report may be stated satisfactory only if total emissions are not materially misstated.
findings.evidence_excerpt: A statement that the report pursuant to Article 14(3) is satisfactory may be made if, in the opinion of the verifier, the total emissions are not materially misstated.

findings.statement: A 'tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent' means one metric tonne of CO₂ or an amount of any other Annex II greenhouse gas with equivalent global-warming potential — the unit for reporting and surrender.
findings.evidence_excerpt: 'tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent' means one metric tonne of carbon dioxide (CO 2) or an amount of any other greenhouse gas listed in Annex II with an equivalent global-warming potential.

payload.rationale: CP1's assurance_artifact=reconciliation_record is the decisive signal and points squarely at Debate: the same annual Scope 2 CO₂e claim is independently reproduced by two methods (A energy-derived scope2_market_proxy_t and B reported scope2_location_t) and then reconciled into one per-site per-year conclusion with an absolute delta and material-discrepancy flag. This is the textbook Discriminator 2 pattern — one single claim verified twice by independent methods and reconciled into one reported figure — supported directly by dual_method_required=true. Supporting signals reinforce Debate: uncertainty=medium with R2 residual interpretive judgment (unresolved emission-factor provenance PF-006, unapproved gas-type qualifier PF-009, analyst-defined |delta|>5% threshold), assurance_level=elevated, and output_type=qualitative (structured interpretive memo). Coalition is excluded because cross_functional_need=false and cluster_count=1 — one team owns the whole reconciliation, no organisational boundary is crossed, and dual_method_required is explicitly a Debate not a Coalition signal. Direct is disfavoured because the work is not a single mechanical dependent chain: two independent method reads must be surfaced and reconciled, and interpretive residuals remain.

alternatives.why_not: assurance_artifact is reconciliation_record, not single_attestation; the case requires two independent method reads of the same claim to be reconciled, and medium interpretive uncertainty remains — not a clean single mechanical dependent chain.

cross_functional_need=false and cluster_count=1 — one compliance team owns the entire reconciliation with no distributed sign-off across organisational domains. dual_method_required=true is a Debate signal (one claim, two verifications), not a Coalition signal.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: This memo is a compliance-team review deliverable covering a 20-site large-manufacturing portfolio over fiscal years 2022–2024, reconciled per site per year. For each site-year it presents the annual CO₂-equivalent figure computed by two independent methods and cross-checks them, flagging any material discrepancy for follow-up. The regulatory frame is Directive 2003/8*/EC (EU ETS): Annex IV grounds the energy-derived calculation, Article 1*(*) grounds the annual operator-reporting cadence, and Article *(j) grounds the tonne-of-CO₂-equivalent unit. Note the approved R2 findings (R2F-001) do not establish that any site is a regulated ETS installation, and several sites (in the US, Canada, China, Serbia, Russia) sit outside the EU ETS geographical scope; the Directive methodology is applied here as an analyst cross-check, not a formal regulatory filing.

sections.heading: Methodology
sections.body: Two independent methods are compared. Method A (energy-derived, Annex IV) computes an emissions proxy as amount_consumed_mwh × co2_factor over Scope 2 rows (scope2_market_proxy_t). Method B (reported, Art. 14(*)) surfaces the directly reported Scope 2 figure (scope2_location_t) on the annual grain. A discrepancy is flagged when the absolute delta exceeds *% of the higher value. Importantly, per R2F-002 that *% threshold is an analyst construct, not a Directive-defined verification test, so a flag is a review trigger rather than a compliance failure. A significant limitation across the portfolio is that the co2_factor / emission factor embedded in the Method A proxy was not independently surfaced (PF-006 unresolved), and the operator's monitoring-plan basis was outside approved scope — so where the two methods match exactly, this often reflects a shared underlying computation rather than an independent cross-confirmation.

sections.heading: Portfolio Results
sections.body: The portfolio comprises 5* site-year entries across 2* sites. Of these, <10 entries are flagged with a discrepancy above the *% threshold, and all * are judged reader-facing material: Business Unit 6 CHE FY2022 (5.7*%), Business Unit 2 Wien FY2022 (9.*%), Business Unit 7 SIMEA Sibiu FY2023 (37.*%, the largest divergence), and Business Unit 2 Kragujevac FY2023 (28.*%). For the remaining entries the two methods agree closely — the large majority within roughly *%, with many exact matches that should be read as source-consistency rather than verification. A material share of entries return exactly zero on both methods (notably the Krefeld, Graz, Peterborough, Wildenrath, ****, and Penig series, plus FY2024 collapses at Berlin, **** and Sibiu); the upstream chain reads these zeros as data-completeness artefacts — absent activity data or possible market-based/non-report positions — rather than confirmed nil emissions.

sections.heading: Limitations
sections.body: This is a monitoring-assurance memo for compliance-team review, not a formal regulatory filing. No figure here should be treated as a Directive-grounded verification outcome. The four flagged discrepancies and the numerous zero-valued site-years require operator-level follow-up before reliance, and the unverifiable emission factors mean neither method can be affirmatively substantiated against Annex IV or Article 1*(*) from the approved data.
